data.formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem yuleSimon_tail (ρ : ℝ) (hρ : 0 < ρ) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun k : ℕ => yuleSimonPMF ρ k)
        (fun k : ℕ => C / (k : ℝ) ^ (ρ + 1)) := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
data.natural_language_statement:
For every $\rho>0$ there is a constant $C>0$ such that the Yule–Simon frequencies $f(k;\rho)=\rho\,B(k,\rho+1)$ satisfy
$$f(k;\rho)\sim\frac{C}{k^{\rho+1}}\qquad(k\to\infty),$$
i.e. $f(k;\rho)\,k^{\rho+1}/C\to1$.
data.source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law), snapshot uploaded by the proposer, section "Related laws" ("The tail frequencies of the Yule–Simon distribution are approximately f(k;ρ) ≈ [constant]/k^(ρ+1) for any choice of ρ > 0").

For every real $\rho>0$ there exists a real $C>0$ such that, as $k\to\infty$ through the naturals, $\mathrm{yuleSimonPMF}(\rho,k)$ is asymptotically equivalent (Lean `IsEquivalent`: the difference is little-o of the second function) to $C/k^{\rho+1}$ (real power). Here $\mathrm{yuleSimonPMF}(\rho,k)=\rho\,\Gamma(k)\Gamma(\rho+1)/\Gamma(k+\rho+1)$.
